The employment outlook will be Good for veterinarians (NOC 31103) in New Brunswick for the 2025-2027 period.

The following factors contributed to this outlook:

  • Employment growth will lead to several new positions.
  • Not many positions will become available due to retirements.
  • Veterinarians are usually employed by farmers, aquaculture facilities, and animal hospitals. Self-employment is also common in this occupation, and many veterinarians run their own clinics. 
  • Veterinarian shortages—in both the small and farm animal fields—have been an issue throughout the province. Increasing numbers of pet adoptions and livestock will continue to support demand for this occupation, but limited training positions in the veterinary college in Atlantic Canada means that these professionals are in limited supply. 
  • A Doctor of Veterinary Medicine degree and registration with the New Brunswick Veterinary Medical Association is required.
  • Employment opportunities will be greater for individuals who are available to work in rural areas and have access to a vehicle, as veterinarians working with livestock often need to travel to and from various farms. However, veterinary clinics for small animals are often located in the province’s major urban areas.
  • These jobs are typically physically demanding, as veterinarians often need to lift heavy animals.
  • Opportunities will be greater for those who are willing to work a flexible schedule, as working evenings, weekends, and holidays is common. Some veterinarians are also required to be on-call in case of emergencies.
